name: Abū al-ʿIrfān Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī al-Ṣabbān
summary: Azhar scholar whose Ḥāshiya on al-Ushmūnī's commentary is the last great work on the Alfiyya, still read in Cairo.
bio: Al-Ṣabbān learnt and taught at al-Azhar in the eighteenth century and wrote on grammar, rhetoric, logic, prosody and the Prophet's life. His Ḥāshiyat al-Ṣabbān ʿalā Sharḥ al-Ushmūnī goes through al-Ushmūnī's commentary phrase by phrase, settling its difficulties with the views of the earlier commentators, and has been printed again and again, with al-ʿAynī's explanation of the evidence verses in the margin. He died in Cairo in 1206/1792.
